questions.answer: B) Libero

questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of the antenna attached to the net in Volleyball?
options: B) To mark the lateral boundaries of the crossing space
C) To secure the net to the poles
D) To assist the setter's alignment
questions.answer: B) To mark the lateral boundaries of the crossing space

questions.question_text: Explain the purpose and basic setup of a block in Volleyball. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A block is a defensive play at the net where front-row players jump with extended arms to intercept an opponent's spiked ball, preventing it from crossing.

questions.question_text: Describe the penhold grip configuration in Table Tennis. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The penhold grip involves holding the racket handle between the thumb and index finger, similar to holding a pen. It provides excellent wrist flexibility for forehand attacks.

questions.question_text: State the therapeutic benefits of practicing Tadasana (Mountain Pose). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Tadasana improves overall body posture, strengthens the thighs, knees, and ankles, relieves tension in the spine, and helps in cultivating physical grounding and mental focus.

questions.question_text: What is the specific rule for tossing the ball during a Table Tennis serve? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: During a serve, the ball must rest freely on the open palm and be tossed nearly vertically upwards at least 16 centimeters without imparting any spin before striking.

questions.question_text: Define the forearm pass or 'dig' technique in Volleyball. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A dig is a defensive pass executed by joining the forearms together to create a flat platform, usually used to receive hard-driven spikes or fast serves.

questions.question_text: Outline the critical alignment and mechanics required to execute a powerful smash in volleyball. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: A powerful smash requires a three-step aggressive approach to build momentum, transferring kinetic energy into a vertical jump. The player must align their hitting shoulder with the ball, snapping the wrist downward at the peak of their jump.

questions.question_text: Explain the therapeutic mechanics and posture of Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose). [30-40 words]
questions.answer: In Bhujangasana, the practitioner lies prone and gently lifts the chest using back muscle strength while keeping the pelvis grounded. This arching mechanic expands the rib cage, deeply stretches the abdominal muscles, and therapeutically strengthens the lower spine.

questions.question_text: Describe how topspin dynamics affect the trajectory and bounce of a Table Tennis ball. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Topspin creates downward Magnus force, causing the ball to dip rapidly in flight and strike the opponent's side faster. Upon bouncing, it shoots forward with accelerated speed and low trajectory, making it highly difficult to counter-attack effectively.

questions.question_text: How does the rotation system function in a standard Volleyball match? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: When a receiving team wins the rally and earns the right to serve, its players must rotate exactly one position in a clockwise direction. This mandatory shift ensures all players participate in both front-row attacking and back-row defending.

questions.question_text: Analyze how incorporating core asanas and mindfulness meditation can therapeutically correct postural deformities and enhance recovery for a student after an intense net game tournament. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Core asanas actively stretch tight hamstrings and realign compressed spinal discs caused by the repetitive jumping and lunging of net games. Holding these poses therapeutically flushes out lactic acid, while mindfulness meditation lowers cortisol levels, promoting deep muscular relaxation. Together, they restore musculoskeletal balance and significantly accelerate the student's physical recovery phase.

questions.question_text: Describe the synchronized defensive mechanics a volleyball team must deploy to effectively counter a coordinated spike attack from the opposing team's front row. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Defending a spike requires immediate synchronization between front-row blockers and back-row defenders. Two front-row players must form a solid double block by timing their vertical jump to intercept the ball's trajectory. Simultaneously, back-row players must lower their center of gravity and read the attacker's shoulder angle to dig any ball deflected past the block.
